Basic ATC

Salire e mantenere

Instruction for the aircraft to begin climbing to the stated altitude and maintain that altitude when reached.

Quick answer: Instruction for the aircraft to begin climbing to the stated altitude and maintain that altitude when reached.

Why it matters

Salire e mantenere matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Salire e mantenere?

In this glossary, Salire e mantenere refers to: Instruction for the aircraft to begin climbing to the stated altitude and maintain that altitude when reached.

How is Salire e mantenere used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "United 357, sali e mantieni livello di volo tre due zero."

Why does Salire e mantenere matter in aviation?

Salire e mantenere matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Salire e mantenere?

Salire e mantenere is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Salire e mantenere belong to?

In this glossary, Salire e mantenere is grouped under Basic ATC. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

Instruction for the aircraft to begin climbing to the stated altitude and maintain that altitude when reached.

Operational example

United 357, climb and maintain flight level three two zero.

Localized term
